standard_prerequisites.name: Representability hypotheses for f and g
standard_prerequisites.statement: A_g represents g (both existence and uniqueness universals) and A_f represents f likewise.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both uniqueness universals are the raw material; the proof is a logical composition of the two.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1146-1150): if h(n) = m with h = f after g, then Q proves forall z (A_h(num n, z) -> z = num m).
Composition (proof lines 1152-1164): write A_h(n, z) as exists y (A_g(n, y) and A_f(y, z)); the two uniqueness universals for g and f compose by logic into forall z (exists y (...) -> z = num m).
proof_roadmap: Unfold A_h by its definition as the existential composition.
Chain the two uniqueness universals for g and f.
Compose by logic into the single universal for z.
difficulty_reason: Uniqueness half of composition (statement 1146-1150, proof 1152-1164): complete logical composition of the two given uniqueness universals, displayed as an align chain. H2.
